product_overview: Folio is a scholarly manuscript submission and peer-review workspace for a single academic journal. It supports the editorial lifecycle from author registration and submission through review, notifications, and public publication, with bilingual UI support and optional AI-assisted workflows.
core_goals: Enable authors to register, authenticate, and manage manuscript submissions
Support editorial review workflows, including submission status management and reviewer assignments
Allow reviewers to accept invitations and submit structured peer reviews
Provide authenticated in-app notifications for workflow events and updates
Expose a public catalog of published submissions for readers
Maintain a stable health endpoint for operational monitoring

features.name: Authentication
features.description: Allows users to register, log in, and view their authenticated profile.
user_flows: POST /api/v1/auth/register with valid email, password, and displayName -> Receive 201 with created AuthUser -> POST /api/v1/auth/login with the same credentials -> Receive 200 with JWT cookies and AuthUser -> GET /api/v1/auth/me with session cookie -> Receive 200 with current User profile
POST /api/v1/auth/login with invalid credentials -> Receive 401 Invalid credentials
POST /api/v1/auth/register with missing or invalid required fields -> Receive validation error response

features.name: Submissions workflow
features.description: Lets authenticated authors create draft submissions, inspect details, submit manuscripts for editorial review, and lets editors update workflow status.
user_flows: POST /api/v1/submissions with authenticated author session -> Receive 201 with new Submission draft -> GET /api/v1/submissions/:slug with session cookie -> Receive 200 with submission detail -> POST /api/v1/submissions/:slug/submit -> Receive 200 with updated Submission in submitted status

GET /api/v1/submissions with authenticated editor session -> Receive 200 with Submission[] for the editor queue -> PATCH /api/v1/submissions/:slug/status with a valid workflow transition -> Receive 200 with updated Submission status
POST /api/v1/submissions/:slug/submit for a submission that fails required validation or is blocked by email verification -> Receive error response such as EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED or validation failure

features.name: Review assignments
features.description: Allows reviewers to see their invitations, accept assignments, and submit peer reviews.
user_flows: GET /api/v1/assignments/me with authenticated reviewer session -> Receive 200 with ReviewAssignment[] -> POST /api/v1/assignments/:slug/accept -> Receive 200 with accepted ReviewAssignment -> POST /api/v1/assignments/:slug/reviews with recommendation and comments -> Receive 201 with created Review
GET /api/v1/assignments/me with no authenticated session -> Receive 401 Unauthorized
POST /api/v1/assignments/:slug/reviews with missing recommendation or comments -> Receive validation error response
POST /api/v1/assignments/:slug/accept when the reviewer email is not verified -> Receive error response such as EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED

features.name: Notifications
features.description: Provides authenticated users with an in-app notification inbox and unread count.
user_flows: GET /api/v1/notifications with authenticated session -> Receive 200 with paginated NotificationPage -> GET /api/v1/notifications/unread-count -> Receive 200 with { count: number }
GET /api/v1/notifications/unread-count with invalid or expired session -> Receive 401 Unauthorized

features.name: Public publications
features.description: Exposes the public catalog of published submissions for unauthenticated readers.
user_flows: GET /api/v1/public/submissions without authentication -> Receive 200 with PublicSubmission[]
GET /api/v1/public/submissions with an empty published catalog -> Receive 200 with an empty array
GET /api/v1/public/submissions with malformed query parameters -> Receive validation or request error response

features.name: Health
features.description: Provides a lightweight liveness check for service monitoring and operational readiness.
user_flows: GET /api/v1/health without authentication -> Receive 200 with { status: ok }
GET /api/v1/health when the service is unavailable -> Receive network or gateway failure instead of 200
